question: What will the Arctic sea ice extent be on September 19, 2026, according to the NSIDC Sea Ice Index?
resolution_criteria: Resolves to the daily Arctic sea ice extent for 2026-09-19 in the NSIDC Sea Ice Index version 4 daily file (N_seaice_extent_daily_v4.0.csv), in millions of square kilometers.
research:
# Arctic sea ice extent on 2026-09-19 (NSIDC Sea Ice Index v4): research notes

## 1. Resolution source
- The question settles on the 2026-09-19 row of the NSIDC daily file. I fetched the file directly. Below are only the values for days through 2026-09-04, the latest data that would have been out by today. Recent daily values (million km²) [NSIDC CSV](https://noaadata.apps.nsidc.org/NOAA/G02135/north/daily/data/N_seaice_extent_daily_v4.0.csv):
  - 2026-08-16: 5.334
  - 2026-08-21: 5.265
  - 2026-08-25: 4.998
  - 2026-08-28: 4.960
  - 2026-08-31: 4.838
  - 2026-09-01: 4.733
  - 2026-09-02: 4.674
  - 2026-09-03: 4.656, the lowest so far this season
  - 2026-09-04: 4.690, the latest value
- Caveat: these are near-real-time values and NSIDC can revise them slightly.
- Recent pace: extent fell about 0.15 per week in late August (5.117 on 08-22 to 4.838 on 08-31), then roughly levelled off from 09-02 to 09-04.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. The latest value, 4.690 on 2026-09-04, sits inside the question's range of 4.2 to 5.15, slightly below the middle.
- Melt has clearly slowed, which fits the usual timing of the annual minimum (around September 10 to 20).
- The September 2026 Sea Ice Index ranking puts this year well behind the record-low years 2012, 2020 and 2019 for early September.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- I could not find an NSIDC "Arctic Sea Ice News" post from August or early September 2026.
- Early September 2026 (exact date unclear): Copernicus reported that August 2026 extent averaged about 6.1 million km². That is 9.2% below the 1991-2020 average and the 12th lowest for August. The largest shortfalls were north of Franz Josef Land and Severnaya Zemlya. [Copernicus](https://climate.copernicus.eu/sea-ice-cover-august-2026)
- August 2026: the UK Met Office, using a different dataset (OSI SAF), put extent at 7.02 million km² on August 2, 9th lowest for that date. It said cool weather was slowing melt. [Met Office Aug briefing](https://www.metoffice.gov.uk/research/approach/monitoring/sea-ice/2026/briefing-on-arctic--antarctic-sea-ice---august-2026)
- March 2026: the winter maximum tied the record low (NASA/NSIDC). [NASA](https://science.nasa.gov/earth/arctic-winter-sea-ice-2026/)

## 4. Base rates
Change in the NSIDC daily value from Sept 4 to Sept 19, read from the same CSV, and what each year's change would give if applied to 2026's 4.690:

| Year | Sep 4 | Sep 19 | Change | Applied to 4.690 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2016 | 4.259 | 4.512 | +0.253 | 4.94 |
| 2017 | 4.826 | 4.751 | -0.075 | 4.62 |
| 2018 | 4.880 | 4.663 | -0.217 | 4.47 |
| 2019 | 4.328 | 4.244 | -0.084 | 4.61 |
| 2020 | 3.908 | 3.865 | -0.043 | 4.65 |
| 2021 | 5.073 | 4.886 | -0.187 | 4.50 |
| 2022 | 4.908 | 4.706 | -0.202 | 4.49 |
| 2023 | 4.469 | 4.253 | -0.216 | 4.47 |
| 2024 | 4.286 | 4.301 | +0.015 | 4.71 |
| 2025 | 4.677 | 4.768 | +0.091 | 4.78 |

- Over these 10 years, the average change was about -0.07 and the median about -0.08. Changes ranged from -0.22 to +0.25. Seven of the ten years ended lower on Sept 19 than on Sept 4. [NSIDC CSV](https://noaadata.apps.nsidc.org/NOAA/G02135/north/daily/data/N_seaice_extent_daily_v4.0.csv)
- Applying those changes to 2026 gives roughly 4.47 to 4.94, with a median near 4.61.
- Daily minimums in recent years and their dates:
  - 2016: 4.145 (Sep 7)
  - 2017: 4.635 (Sep 13)
  - 2018: 4.630 (Sep 21)
  - 2019: 4.166 (Sep 18)
  - 2020: 3.793 (Sep 13)
  - 2021: 4.757 (Sep 14)
  - 2023: 4.244 (Sep 17)
  - 2024: 4.245 (Sep 10)
  - 2025: 4.543 (Sep 8)
- Once the minimum has passed, the refreeze often adds 0.05 to 0.25 by Sept 19 (for example 2016 and 2025). If the minimum comes late, the Sept 19 value can still be near the season's low (2018, 2019, 2023).
- Even in the late-season weeks, the daily series moves up and down by about ±0.03 to 0.05 from one day to the next.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Polymarket ran a market on the 2026 summer minimum (lowest NSIDC daily value from Aug 1 to Oct 1). The only prices I found were stale snapshots from late May and early June 2026, roughly 39% to 57% for a minimum below 4.0. I found no current price before Sept 5. [ClearMarket mirror](https://clearmarket-1dg.pages.dev/events/min-arctic-sea-ice-extent-this-summer/), [orrery](https://orrery.me/markets/will-the-minimum-arctic-sea-ice-extent-this-summer-be-at-least-5m-square-kilometers)
- Kalshi and Manifold have threshold markets on the minimum (Manifold cites Kalshi thresholds of 3.6 to 4.8). I found no current price for either. [Manifold](https://manifold.markets/prismatic/which-arctic-sea-ice-minimum-thresh)
- Sea Ice Prediction Network (SIPN) July 2026 outlook, as reported second-hand: median 4.45 million km² for September average extent, interquartile range 4.20 to 4.67. Note this is a monthly average, not a daily value. I could not find the August SIPN report itself. [Met Office forecasts page](https://www.metoffice.gov.uk/research/climate/seasonal-to-decadal/seasonal-forecast/arctic-sea-ice)
- Met Office June 2026 collection of forecasts: median 4.83, from 18 estimates ranging from 4.22 to 5.18.
- I found no forecast aimed specifically at the Sept 19 daily value.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- NSIDC normally announces the annual minimum in mid to late September. A preliminary announcement could come before Sept 20.
- Weather from Sept 5 to 19 will drive the outcome. Storms or winds that spread the ice out or push it together, and Pacific-side warmth, can move extent by ±0.1 to 0.2 within days.
- The SIPN September report is due in late September, after resolution.
- The value for 09-19 should appear in the CSV around Sept 20. Near-real-time values can be revised by about ±0.01 to 0.03.
